who: The Buddha · Majjhima Nikaya 36, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: But I have not achieved any superhuman distinction... by this severe, grueling work. Could there be another path to awakening?
meaning: Pushing harder and harder did not work. So he asked: is there another way? He found a gentler one.

who: Thomas Edison, as told by Walter S. Mallory · Dyer & Martin, 1910
quote: Results! Why, man, I have gotten a lot of results! I know several thousand things that won't work.
meaning: Every failed test showed him one more way that does not work. No test was wasted.

quote: Ch'iu is retiring and slow; therefore, I urged him forward. Yu has more than his own share of energy; therefore, I kept him back.
meaning: Same question, two answers. He pushed the shy student forward and held the eager one back.

who: Nanyue Huairang to his student Mazu · tr. D. T. Suzuki, 1927
quote: It is like driving a cart; when it moveth not, wilt thou whip the cart or the ox?
meaning: If the cart won't move, hitting the cart is useless. Find what really pulls it, and work there.

who: Dick Fosbury · high jumper, Athletics Weekly, 2018
quote: All the time I was doing it by feel as there was no model to follow. I was creating it as I went.
meaning: The usual jump did not work for him. He trusted his feel and made a new one.

who: Orville & Wilbur Wright · The Century Magazine, 1908
quote: Having set out with absolute faith in the existing scientific data, we were driven to doubt one thing after another, till finally, after two years of experiment, we cast it all aside, and decided to rely entirely upon our own investigations.
meaning: The old numbers kept failing them. So they tested everything themselves, and then they flew.

who: Little Roadling (Culla-Panthaka) · Jataka No. 4, tr. T. W. Rhys Davids, 1880
quote: ...in four months he could not get by heart even this one verse... gave him a piece of very white cloth... and said, 'Now, Little Roadling... rub this cloth up and down...'
meaning: He could not learn one verse in four months. The Buddha gave him a cloth to rub instead. It worked.

who: Epictetus · Enchiridion 43, tr. Thomas W. Higginson, 1865
quote: Everything has two handles: one by which it may be borne, another by which it cannot... and thus you will lay hold on it as it is to be borne.
meaning: Every hard thing has two handles. If you can't carry it one way, hold it by the other.

quote: Build the house to suit the one who lives in it...
meaning: Fit the way to the person.

who: The Buddha to Sona · Anguttara Nikaya 6.55, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: When your harp’s strings were tuned too tight, was it resonant and playable?” ... “In the same way, Sona, when energy is too forceful it leads to restlessness. When energy is too slack it leads to laziness.
meaning: Too tight or too loose, the harp makes no music. Your effort needs the same balance.
